raw.body:
**Follow-up: the recovery this bug forces can itself crash fatally (`commitOffscreenPassiveMountEffects`)**

One more data point on severity. We caught the following uncaught TypeError in production, in exactly the session profile this issue describes — hard load of a PPR shell+resume product route, burst delivery, seven `#418`s in the preceding second (i.e. the SSR discard described above), then:

```
TypeError: Cannot create property 'refCount' on number '0'
    at commitOffscreenPassiveMountEffects (react-dom-client.production.js:11205:41)
    at recursivelyTraverseReconnectPassiveEffects (react-dom-client.production.js:11440 / 11467 / 11494)
    ... (~47 recursive reconnect frames — a deep hidden→visible reveal traversal)
```

react-dom `19.3.0-canary-3f0b9e61-20260317` (vendored in next 16.2.9), `cacheComponents: true`.

Reading the minified bundle, the throw site is the cache-pool retention in `commitOffscreenPassiveMountEffects`:

```js
current = null;
null !== finishedWork.memoizedState &&
  null !== finishedWork.memoizedState.cachePool &&
  (current = finishedWork.memoizedState.cachePool.pool);
current !== previousCache &&
  (null != current && current.refCount++,   // ← throws: current === 0
   null != previousCache && releaseCache(previousCache));
```

So the Offscreen fiber's `memoizedState.cachePool.pool` held the **number `0`** rather than a `Cache` object (or null) — a lanes-shaped value sitting where a cache belongs, which smells like internal stack-cursor misalignment during the mismatch-recovery unwind/re-render. It surfaced during the passive-effects reconnect traversal of the client re-render that followed the `#418` storm.

Because it throws in the commit phase, it is not recoverable: the nearest error boundary takes the route down. So the failure mode of this issue isn't limited to "SSR discarded + client re-render" — the forced recovery can kill the page entirely.

Observed once so far (headless Chromium 149, hard load); no standalone repro — it's evidently rare even among corrupted loads (our 10/10 burst repros never hit it). Happy to share the full Sentry event (breadcrumbs, all 50 frames) if useful. Arguably a distinct react-dom bug in its own right — recovery should never corrupt the cache pool regardless of what triggered the mismatch — so I can split it into a separate issue if you'd prefer.
